title: Extract the duplicated, inconsistently-patched _extractFirebaseCode helper into one shared function
why: The same '_extractFirebaseCode' helper is copy-pasted across 4 files in this batch (plus a 5th in features/settings/presentation/screens/upgrade_to_cloud_screen.dart, outside it) and the copies have drifted: sign_in_controller.dart's own comment documents that the original pattern `\[([a-z-]+)\]` fails to match Firebase's real `[plugin/code]` format (e.g. `[firebase_auth/wrong-password]`), silently degrading every mapped error to the generic 'Sign-in failed' message — and fixed it locally. magic_link_service.dart and upgrade_to_cloud_service.dart still carry that exact stale pattern, so an email-already-in-use or wrong-password condition surfacing through either of those paths still silently falls through to a generic error today.
recommendation: Extract one shared helper (e.g. core/auth/firebase_error_code.dart, consistent with Rule 3's core/auth placement for Firebase-adjacent parsing) using sign_in_controller.dart's fixed pattern, and delete the other 4 copies (in and out of this batch).
acceptance_criteria: A unit test on the shared helper asserts it extracts the code from both '[code]' and '[plugin/code]' shapes
AG-4 duplicate-symbol grep no longer finds multiple _extractFirebaseCode definitions

corrections: The claimed consequence ('email-already-in-use or wrong-password... falls through to generic error') does not apply to magic_link_service.dart, whose only _extractFirebaseCode call site (line 221) checks 'invalid-action-code'/'expired-action-code' for internal pref cleanup, not password/email-collision codes. The real second half of that reachable bug chain is features/settings/presentation/screens/upgrade_to_cloud_screen.dart (mentioned only as an aside 'outside' the batch), which has the identical stale regex and IS used for user-facing error mapping.
